**Instructions.** Complete this assignment in Quarto or R Markdown and submit
a rendered PDF to Gradescope. Show your code. Interpretation questions are
graded on precision (adjusted for what, units, association vs causation,
population), exactly as practiced in the labs. End with your AI-use statement
(see Section 4).

**Data.** The Stanford prostate cancer study: 97 men about to receive a
radical prostatectomy, with pre-surgery measurements:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data(prostate, package = "faraway")
```

Variables used below: `lpsa` = log of prostate-specific antigen (PSA, log
ng/ml), `lcavol` = log cancer volume (log cm^3^), `lweight` = log prostate
weight (log g), `age` = age (years), `svi` = seminal vesicle invasion
(1 = yes, 0 = no). Note that the outcome and two predictors are on the log
scale; interpret their coefficients in log units.

# Section 1: Do (6 points)

**1.1** Describe the outcome `lpsa`: a histogram plus a short numerical
summary. Two sentences on center, spread, and shape, remembering the units
are log ng/ml. (2 pts)

**1.2** Fit the multiple regression of `lpsa` on `lcavol`, `lweight`, `age`,
and `svi`. Report the coefficient table (estimates, standard errors, t values,
p-values) and the residual standard error. (2 pts)

**1.3** Report 95% confidence intervals for all coefficients using
`confint()`. State which intervals exclude zero. (2 pts)

# Section 2: Interpret (8 points; interpretation precision counts double)

**2.1** Write the strong-form interpretation of the `svi` coefficient in one
sentence, incorporating its confidence interval. Remember: `svi` is binary,
the outcome is log PSA, and the sentence must state the adjustment set, the
comparison being made, association wording, and the population. (2 pts)

**2.2** The confidence interval for `age` contains zero. Write two sentences
giving the correct interpretation of this interval: what range of age
associations is compatible with the data, and what the interval does and does
not allow you to conclude. (2 pts)

**2.3** Test whether `age` and `lweight` jointly add anything beyond `lcavol`
and `svi`: fit the reduced model `lpsa ~ lcavol + svi` and compare it to the
full model with `anova()`. State the null hypothesis of this F test in words,
report F and the p-value, and give your conclusion in one sentence. (2 pts)

**2.4** Your answers to 2.2 and 2.3 may feel like they pull in opposite
directions: `age` looks unimportant on its own, yet the pair (`age`,
`lweight`) is jointly significant. In two or three sentences, reconcile this
using the distinction between statistical and practical significance and the
difference between individual and joint tests. Which single variable is doing
the work in the joint test, and how can you tell from the coefficient table?
(2 pts)

# Section 3: Critique the AI (6 points)

A student pasted this dataset description into an AI assistant and asked for
an inference write-up. The assistant replied:

> "I fit `lpsa ~ lcavol + lweight + age + svi` on the 97 patients. The 95%
> confidence interval for `age` was (-0.030, 0.012); because this interval
> contains zero, we know the true effect of age is zero, so dropping age
> changes nothing. The p-value for `svi` was 0.002, meaning there is a 99.8%
> probability that seminal vesicle invasion affects PSA. Comparing
> `lpsa ~ lcavol + svi` against the full model, `anova()` gave F = 6.11 with
> p = 0.003, which proves that `age` and `lweight` each individually improve
> the model. Also, `lcavol`'s t statistic of 7.43 is more than double `svi`'s
> 3.17, so cancer volume has more than twice as large an effect on PSA as
> seminal vesicle invasion. Age itself was clearly irrelevant (p = 0.52)."

**3.1** This paragraph contains at least four distinct statistical errors.
Identify each one you find (quote the offending phrase), and explain in one
or two sentences why it is wrong. Finding four earns full credit; a fifth
earns a bonus point. (4 pts + 1 bonus)

**3.2** Verify the AI's inference claims about `age` by fitting the models
yourself. Report the actual p-value for `age` in the full model and the
actual F and p-value from the nested `anova()` comparison, state which of the
AI's numbers do not match, and write the correct one-sentence conclusion
about what the joint test does and does not show. (2 pts)

# Section 4: AI-use statement (required, ungraded)

One or two sentences: which AI tools you used on this assignment and for what,
or "No AI tools used." Note that Section 3 asks you to critique provided AI
output; using an AI to critique the AI is permitted, but the errors you report
are yours to defend.
